description_en: Aśikharatemple on top of a fountain and a stone memorial pillar from circa 14th-15th century.The monument is located in the south-eastern end of the village of Bhām Bāḍā, 1.5 km south of Gamgadhi, the Mugu district headquarters.Theśikharatemple is oriented to the south-east. In front of theśikhara, to the south-east, is a fountain with a stone facing. Fountains are locally known asmugrāhā. The facing is carved with a few mouldings. Water used to come out through two uncarved spouts. Rectangular platforms were placed at the left and right ends of the fountain. These platforms are now missing.The association of aśikharatemple with a fountain is unique in the Dailekh district. It is more commonly found in the Jumla and Mugu districts (see for instanceDLK0100). The Bhām Bāḍā monuments, as well as the otherdevaldharasin the Karnali may be dated between the second half of the 14th century and the 15th century (Andolfatto 2019: 88-89, 101-102).The monument is mentioned inSharma 2012: 194-195 andAndolfatto 2019: 86.
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne University, 2019. Sharma, Dilli Raj. Heritage of Western Nepal. Art and Architecture . Kathmandu: Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies, 2012.
